'''Dansein''' is one of the Sub-Districts of Peckern North. The two new development areas within this district is mainly designed for resdiential and commercial use. This area is developed by DaOrangeStoneOre.

History

Dansein Market

Dansein was originally named "K-Paifay", and a station was set up by Cities Transport Railway Division on December 2017. However, due to the fact that the Chinese name of that area had innuendos, the station at that area was re-named Dansein Market Station on September 2018. Afterwards, residential and commercial development begun around that station, and twelve grids were defined at the area closest to this station. However, the grids have yet to see any development to date.

Subsequent development to the southwest of Dansein Market is the Shek Pai Tau New Town and what will become Tin Kam. While the area developed at the southwest is derived from the potential development in the Dansein Market area, the developer became worried that new town development would affect scenery near Dansein Market.

Gremming

Gremming is a forest located between Dansein Market and Shek Pai Tau New Town, and it may be dervied from the word "Gremlin", which is a "mischievous folkloric creature responsible for malfunctions in aircraft, and later in other machinery, processes, and their operators".

However, the reason why the area was related to "Gremlin" in the first place is in turn related to a certain villager named Gamil who lived in Clearbrook Village. He was wandering around where Gamil Court is today when he suddenly began reminiscing about his life and screamed erratically. Nearby villagers were alerted of this commotion and upon discovering, only to find his body. As a result, that area was named "Gremming" to commemorate the dead villager.

Just a few days after Shek Pai Tau New Town began construction, Gremming Forest was razed down, and in its place were public housing. Currently, this area is riddled with a series of public housing that is home to 76 thousand people. If subsequent construction of private housing were considered, the population of this area totals 160 thousand.

Pan Tin

Named after the Village of Pan Tin Tsuen, the area northwest of Dansein Market was once resided with citizens, known of their elegant lifestyles.

Upon the beginning of development of Dansein, the residents agreed with a compensated transfer of land ownership for residential development, under the conditions of resettlement within the area and a control in residential building counts. With that in mind under comprehensive planning, the upper limit of 39 public residential buildings were set by the developers (by symbolic derivations from the Chinese characters of the name Pan Tin). The planning also included the construction of Pan Tin Court in fulfillment of the resettlement condition.

Following the initializing in development of Northern Dansein New Town, the developers changed their plans to break free of the 39 buildings limit. Though the native residents of Pan Tin welcomed the change, and hoped an increase to the developments of housing developments for home ownership, in combat to the nearby private housing developments.

Currently the west potion of the area is generally completed, while that of the east is still under construction.

Summary

Contrary to the perceived priorities implied by the naming, the surrounding housing development of this area is more well-developed than the centered "market" area.

Future Development

After the facilities for the existing Public Housing Estates are completed, Dansein will expand to the northwest at the outside, and the "Dansein Residential Area" would be further divided into "South Dansein" and "North Dansein" residential areas.

In response to re-development of the nearby Tin Kum-Shek Pai Tau New Town, plans to integrate Dansein and Shek Pai Tau into a larger-scaled Peckern North Metropolis are also in place.

'''Deepond Island''' (Ch: ''深湖洲'', Jp: ''深湖洲''・<small>Fukaumi-shima</small>) is one of the islands on West Metropolis Archipelago. It is located to the south of Inthree Island, the southeast of Axtail Island and the southwest of Coubird-Flask Group. It features a Nazca Railway Station featuring and for external access. However, due to historical reasons, development on this island was temporarily suspended before resuming on May 8 2019.

Location

Deepond Island is located at the northwest of West Metropolis Archipelago. It houses a deep pond named Deepond and is the namesake of this island.

East Pond Reef

East Pond Reef is one of the subsidiary reefs of Deepond Island, and is separated from '''Deepond Island''' by Lighthouse River.

Geological Points of Interest

  • Deepond
  • Hai-Kau River
  • Lighthouse River

Map

Transport Manual

  • Arriving from east Los Sengas:
  • After Using /spawn or arriving at Metropolis Terminal, take to Jayler Station, and then change to before alighting at Deepond Island Station.
  • Passengers from northeast Los Sengas may directly take and alight at Deepond Island Station.
  • Arriving from Peckern, Caver Island, Heeled Island, Stem Island, Note Group, Kneeling Island, Dark Pearl Island:
  • Take to Fansim Island Station, and then change to before alighting at Deepond Island Station.
  • Passengers from Stone Shoal or Stations to the west of it are advised to change to at Stone Shoal Station, before changing to at Gull Woods Station before reaching Fansim Island Station. The rest of the journey is the same as above.
  • Arriving from Axhead Island, Axtail Island, Flask Island, Bufly Island:
  • Tourists are advised to take ships from Nazca Ferry or use the Elytra to fly to the island.
  • Arriving from Threeler, Ponsand Island, Ponrest Island, Peckern North:
  • Tourists are advised to take ships from Nazca Ferry or use the Elytra to fly to the island.
  • Arriving from other stations along , , :
  • Tourists are advised to use to reach to this station.

Sub-Districts

Deepond Island is divided into 10 Sub-Districts as follows:

  • Deepnorth (Japanese:深北町<small>(ふかきたちょう)</small>): Located near Exit B of the Nazca Railway Station, and includes the Nazca Ferry. It was formerly named North Pond, and development of this sub-district is mostly complete save for a few buildings.
  • Grand Pond (Japanese:大湖町<small>(だいこちょう)</small>): Located near the south of Deepnorth to the North coast of Deepond. It is currently planned as a commercial district.
  • The japanese name is named after an area in Neihu District of Taipei with the same name.
  • North Sand (Japanese:北砂町<small>(きたすなちょう)</small>): Located to the west of Deepnorth. It is home to the Deepond Island Government. Its development is mostly complete.
  • Grass Pond (Japanese:草湖町<small>(くさこちょう)</small>): A peninsula to the northwest of Deepond. It is currently planned to be a commercial district.
  • West Pond (Japanese:西湖町<small>(さいこちょう)</small>): Located at the west of Deepond Island and the south of Grass Pond. It is currently planned to have public facilities, including a library, a hospital and a school. It is currently the main development area of the island.
  • The japanese name is named after an area in Neihu District of Taipei with the same name.
  • Star Pond (Japanese:星湖町<small>(ほしみずうみちょう)</small>): Located at the northeast of Deepond Island. it is currently a residential area, and is undergoing re-construction.
  • East Pond (Japanese:東湖町<small>(とうこちょう)</small>): A thin strip of land to the east of Deepond Island. It features a Fish Market, a Post Office and a Campsite. The proposed Route 12 exit is also located here.
  • The japanese name is named after an area in Neihu District of Taipei with the same name.
  • East Coast (Japanese:東岸町<small>(とうがんちょう)</small>): A new reclaimation area to the east of Star Pond. It features a lighthouse and a market. It is planned to be a commercial-residential district in the future.
  • Gravies (Japanese:グラビ): Located at the south of Deepond Island. Formerly named South Pond, this area is planned to be a residential district, and is currently one of the main development areas. It is also home to Deepond Light Rail's depot.
  • The english name is named after the first area developed by Haruna City Railway on February 2015.
  • Godplains/Kamibara (Japanese:神原町<small>(かみばらちょう)</small>): A shoal located at the southeast of Deepond Island. It is the tourist hotspot of Deepond Island, and is also home to the bus terminal.

Transport

Nazca Railway

  • , Deepond Island Station

Deepond Light Rail

Besides of Nazca Railway, another major transport infrastructure within Deepond Island is the Deepond Light Rail. Deepond Light Rail is an in-district rail system operated jointly by the Deepond Island Government and the Deepond Light Rail Management Company. Currently, it is under re-construction.

Maritime Transport

  • At the north of this island, the Deepond Island Pier ran by Nazca Ferry Co. Ltd. is constructed, and is colloquially named "North Pier". Passengers can use this pier to reach islands such as Coubird-Flask Group, Droplet Island, Axhead Island, Axtail Island and Bufly Island.
  • At the south of this island, the Gravies Street Pier is also present. It is currently a historic site of Deepond Island. To the south of this island is a freight terminal which is colloquially named "South Pier".

Roads

  • Beneath this island, a Public Transport Interchange for Route 12 is constructed, with a station (Route 12 Entrance Station) that is served by Deepond Light Rail and will be served by .

Buses

Deepond Underground Walkway

Deepond Underground Walkway is constructed by the Deepond Island Government in order to help citizens adopt to the adverse weather. However, due to redevelopment, most of the underground walkway have been demolished.

Points of Interest

Future Development

Deepond Island will become a mid-density residential area complete with its own underground walkway and sewer systems.
